title: No Verified Incident Can Justify Vietnam’s Dog-Trade Defenses
excerpt: No verified seizure, conviction, location, or health alert is documented here. Claims about dog farms, stolen pets, and disease cannot replace evidence or justify trade protections.
body_html:
Claims about stolen pets, poison bait, illegal transport, and contaminated meat demand serious investigation. But no verified incident, court judgment, police seizure, location, date, named agency, or health alert is documented in the material available here. That gap matters. Public anger must target proven cruelty and criminal networks, not unsupported claims.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

“Farm-raised dogs” is a claim requiring records: licensed premises, animal identification, transport documents, veterinary inspection, quarantine compliance, and slaughter oversight. Without transparent records, buyers and authorities cannot distinguish lawful activity from stolen-companion trafficking or unquarantined movement. That is a regulatory failure, not proof that every operator commits a crime.

Health risk needs precise language

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance supports these medical facts.

Evidence first. Abolition through public mandate.

Vietnamese families, pet owners, veterinarians, and local leaders deserve enforcement based on documented offenses and transparent inspection. The SDE campaign demand goes further: complete national abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, and follow campaign updates as that demand reaches decision-makers.

facebook_post:
Rabies control cannot stop at household gates—but public trust cannot rest on unverified stories either.

Claims about cyanide bait, stolen family dogs, illegal transport, and “farm-raised” animals require dates, locations, named agencies, seizure records, court judgments, and veterinary evidence. None are documented in the material currently available here. That does not excuse cruelty or weak regulation. It demands an investigation strong enough to protect Vietnamese families, pets, and communities without inventing victims or blaming culture.

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care. Vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies must be given before symptoms develop. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal.

Vietnamese communities can demand traceability, quarantine enforcement, action against pet theft, and complete abolition by 2030. Evidence makes reform stronger. Public solidarity makes it possible.
